source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
Citrus greening disease, also called citrus decline (Huanglongbing/HLB), is caused by a bacteria-like organism that lives in the phloem (the nutrient-conducting tissue) of the tree. As the pathogen builds up, it blocks the tree's own nutrient transport, producing yellow, mottled leaves that can resemble a nutrient deficiency. Affected trees show progressively more yellowing over time, stop producing fruit well, and in general decline toward death if untreated.

Control measures given in the source:
1) Cut off and burn/destroy affected branches -- do not leave infected material in the orchard.
2) Only propagate new trees from budwood/scion material taken from confirmed disease-free mother trees.
3) Spray to control the psyllid vector (see the Asian citrus psyllid pest entry): Imidacloprid 70% SL at 8 ml per 20 L water, or Lambda-cyhalothrin 2.5% CS at 15 ml per 20 L water.
